caution: A failure to reproduce is not a finding that the paper is wrong. It may be a failure of the attempt.

attempts.label: DANDI:001516
attempts.paper_title: Sub-microsecond optical measurements of cell membrane charging and lesioning by pulsed electric fields
attempts.entry_title: Membrane charging and recovery after pulsed electric fields (Semenov et al. 2026)
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Semenov, Silkuniene, Silkunas, Pakhomova, Bixler, Ibey, Kochunov and Pakhomov (2026) on dandiset 001516. The dandiset holds a FluoVolt two-pulse experiment in CHO cells, with inter-pulse intervals of 1 to 250 us and fields of 150 to 1570 V/cm, which the paper does not report; none of the recordings behind the paper's figures is in it. The one claim that is a computation from the paper's Eq. (2) is tested, and the dataset's own sets are measured with the paper's pole method.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Semenov et al. (2026) from dandiset 001516

outcomes.statement: With Di-8-ANEPPS and 1-us pulses, polarization grows with field strength up to 570 V/cm; at 780 V/cm the cathodic pole stops increasing and dims, and at 1000 to 1400 V/cm the poles show reduced or absent polarization while regions nearer the equator stay polarized and may polarize more than the poles.
outcomes.source: Figure 1 and its legend; Results 3.1, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: At a higher electric field strength of 780 V/cm, polarization at the cathodic pole does not further increase but dims out, indicating a less efficient charging of the partially permeabilized membrane. Still stronger electric fields produce a distinct pattern of reduced or absent polarization at the poles ... while regions closer to the equator remain relatively intact and may polarize more than the poles
outcomes.notes: The criterion uses the Di-8-ANEPPS 1-us escalation cells of Fig. 4B (n = 5). Every file of the dandiset names FluoVolt, and none holds a 1-us escalation over 43 to 1400 V/cm in sets of 40 and 60 images; the dandiset holds a FluoVolt two-pulse experiment the paper does not report (notebook, data check). Dandisets 001517 and 001518, separate targets with their own claims files, are titled as Di-8-ANEPPS and dye-comparison experiments of the same lab and were not used here.

outcomes.statement: With FluoVolt, pole dF rose with field strength until it saturated at 66% (255 mV) at 360 V/cm at the cathodic pole and -83% (-320 mV) at 570 V/cm at the anodic pole; stronger fields did not increase the anodic response and decreased the cathodic one.
outcomes.quote: ΔF increased proportionally to the electric field strength until reaching apparent saturation at 66% ΔF (255 mV IMP) at 360 V/cm at the cathodic pole, and −83% ΔF (−320 mV IMP) at 570 V/cm at the anodic pole. Further escalation of the electric field strength did not increase the dye response at the anodic pole and even decreased it at the cathodic pole.
outcomes.notes: Needs the FluoVolt escalation of Fig. 2A (n = 4, 43 to 1400 V/cm, 40 baseline and 60 pulse images, with values at 360 and 570 V/cm). The dandiset's only FluoVolt single-pulse sets are two fields of view (c6, c7) at 150, 520, 900, 1270 and 1570 V/cm with 1.00-mm electrodes and 20 and 40 frames, which are not these recordings and have neither 360 nor 570 V/cm. Measured with the paper's method as a variant (no outcome, 4 cells), their pole response with the uniform offset removed is 14.3 to 15.6% at the cathodic pole at 150, 520 and 1570 V/cm and 7.0 to 9.0% at 900 and 1270 V/cm, and peaks at -23.2% at the anodic pole at 520 V/cm.

outcomes.statement: FluoVolt measurements were stable without pulses (no significant bleaching or photosensitization), and the response within each set stayed stable through the 60 pulses, even at 1000 V/cm and above.
outcomes.quote: Without PEF (first 40 datapoints, or ~ 7 s in each set), measurements were stable, indicating no significant photosensitization or dye bleaching ... but the dye response in each set stayed stable through the 60 pulses applied
outcomes.notes: Needs the Fig. 2A FluoVolt escalation cells (n = 4) at 1000 to 1400 V/cm, which are not in the dandiset (see fig2a-fluovolt-saturation). As a variant on the dandiset's own single-pulse sets (c6, c7; 4 cells; no outcome), the criterion's comparison gives a fall of the per-frame pole dF within the 40 pulse frames at 1270 and 1570 V/cm of 2.9 to 11.1 points under reading (b) (3 of 4 pole-sets at p < 0.05) and 3.8 to 24.0 points under reading (a) (1 of 4), and in the sham set a fall of 12.1 and 12.2 points in the pulse frames and 15.9 and 16.3 points in the baseline (frames 1-9 against 10-19) with no pulse. By the claim's rule these recordings would give not reproduced; they are not the paper's cells.

outcomes.statement: Di-8-ANEPPS dF kept increasing with field strength up to 570 V/cm at both poles.
outcomes.quote: This dye has a lower sensitivity to membrane polarization (note the vertical scale different from Fig. 2A), but ΔF kept climbing up to the electric field strength of 570 V/cm at both cell poles.
outcomes.notes: Needs the Di-8-ANEPPS escalation of Fig. 2B (n = 5); all 72 files of the dandiset name FluoVolt.

outcomes.statement: Di-8-ANEPPS responses were somewhat affected by bleaching, most visibly at 43 V/cm, where bleaching added about 5% to dF at the anodic pole and took about 5% from it at the cathodic pole.
outcomes.quote: The responses were somewhat affected by dye bleaching (particularly noticeable at 43 V/cm, where bleaching added ~5% to ΔF at the anodic pole and reduced it by the same ~5% at the cathodic pole.
outcomes.notes: Needs the Di-8-ANEPPS 43 V/cm sets of Fig. 2B; the dandiset holds no Di-8-ANEPPS recording and no 43 V/cm set.

outcomes.statement: With Di-8-ANEPPS, responses to pulses of 780 V/cm and above decreased gradually within each set of 60 images.
outcomes.quote: In addition, responses to PEFs at and above 780 V/cm decreased gradually in each set of 60 images, consistent with expectations of adding membrane damage by additional electroporation pulses in each set
outcomes.notes: Needs the Di-8-ANEPPS sets of Fig. 2B at 780 to 1400 V/cm; not in the dandiset.

outcomes.statement: Repeated alternating sets at 150 and 230 V/cm (480 pulses and 800 flashes) gave dF responses constant within and between sets.
outcomes.quote: Repeated sets of PEFs at 150 and 230 V/cm, delivered in alternation, produced ΔF responses that stayed constant both within each set and between the sets (Fig. 2C and D).
outcomes.notes: Needs the Di-8-ANEPPS alternation of 150 and 230 V/cm sets of Fig. 2C and D (n = 8); the dandiset holds no alternation protocol and no 230 V/cm set.

outcomes.statement: At 1000 V/cm the cathodic pole dF fell from 40 +- 10% at the start of the set to 26.6 +- 8% at its end, a trend that was not statistically significant.
outcomes.quote: In contrast, at an electroporating field strength of 1000 V/cm, ΔF at the cathodic pole decreased from 40 ± 10% at the beginning of the set to 26.6 ± 8% at the end of it. Although not statistically significant (p > 0.05)

statistics.test: 2-tailed paired t-test (named in the Fig. 2 legend)

outcomes.notes: Needs the 1000 V/cm Di-8-ANEPPS set of the Fig. 2C cells (n = 8); not in the dandiset.

outcomes.statement: Set-averaged dF stayed nearly constant before the 1000 V/cm exposure but was about 20% lower in the sets after it.
outcomes.quote: ΔF values averaged across each set of 60 PEFs stayed nearly constant before the electroporation, but dropped by about 20% in the sets acquired after it (Fig. 2D, p < 0.05).
outcomes.notes: Needs the Fig. 2C and D sets before and after 1000 V/cm (n = 8); not in the dandiset.

outcomes.statement: Fitted linearly through the origin over -150 to +150 mV IMPC, FluoVolt changes by 26% and Di-8-ANEPPS by 9.1% dF per 100 mV, with correlation coefficients 0.96 and 0.78.
outcomes.quote: The correlation coefficients of the fits equaled 0.96 for FluoVolt and 0.78 for Di-8 ANEPPS (due to a lower signal-to-noise ratio), with respective slope coefficients of 26% and 9.1% ΔF per 100 mV of IMP.
outcomes.notes: Needs the 43 to 360 V/cm sets of both dyes and the cells' radii in um. The dandiset holds no Di-8-ANEPPS set and no FluoVolt set at 43, 230 or 360 V/cm, and its files give no pixel size, so no radius in um. The outside input (the tau fit of reference [20]) was not pinned, as the recordings it would be applied to are missing.

outcomes.statement: FluoVolt departed from linearity from about +-200 mV IMPC, while Di-8-ANEPPS stayed nearly linear from -500 to +500 mV; so FluoVolt's early departure reflects its dynamic range, not electroporation.
outcomes.quote: The actual measurements with FluoVolt gradually became non-linear already at ±200 mV, while those for Di-8-ANEPPS stayed essentially linear throughout the tested range from −500 to +500 mV.
outcomes.notes: Depends on fig3-dye-sensitivity, blocked for missing data.

outcomes.statement: FluoVolt measured and calculated IMP matched only at 43 and 150 V/cm; with stronger 1-us pulses the pole dF peaked at 71 +- 10% (cathodic) and -83.5 +- 5% (anodic), about +260 and -330 mV.
outcomes.quote: However, this assumption held only for the applied fields of 43 and 150 V/cm, where measured and calculated IMP matched. With stronger PEFs, maximum ΔF reached 71 ± 10% and −83.5 ± 5% at the cathodic and anodic poles, respectively.
outcomes.notes: Needs the Fig. 4A FluoVolt escalation (n = 4, 43 to 1400 V/cm) and the per-cell IMPC; neither the recordings nor a pixel size for the radius are in the dandiset (see fig2a-fluovolt-saturation for the dandiset's own FluoVolt single-pulse sets, measured as a variant).

outcomes.statement: FluoVolt cathodic polarization fell from 71% at 360 V/cm to 45 to 50% at 1000 to 1400 V/cm.
outcomes.quote: Notably, polarization at the cathodic pole decreased from 71% at 360 V/cm to 45–50% at 1000–1400 V/cm, indicating that the more severe membrane damage prevented its polarization to the maximum.
outcomes.notes: Needs the Fig. 4A cells at 360 and 1000 to 1400 V/cm; the dandiset has no 360, 1000, 1200 or 1400 V/cm set. In the dandiset's own single-pulse sets (variant, no outcome, 4 cells) the cathodic response with the offset removed is 14.3% at 150 V/cm, 7.0% at 900, 9.0% at 1270 and 15.6% at 1570 V/cm.

outcomes.statement: With Di-8-ANEPPS and 1-us pulses, measured IMP fell below the calculated value at 570 V/cm, where dF peaked at 57 +- 14% (cathodic) and -55 +- 4% (anodic), over 600 mV.
outcomes.quote: The measured IMP decreased below the calculated value when the electric field reached 570 V/cm, concurrently with reaching the maximum ΔF of 57 ± 14% at the cathodic pole and − 55 ± 4% at the anodic pole. These values corresponded to membrane polarization by over 600 mV, which is twice the value measured with FluoVolt.
outcomes.notes: Needs the Di-8-ANEPPS 1-us escalation of Fig. 4B (n = 5); not in the dandiset.

outcomes.statement: Averaged over only the first 10 of the 60 pulses, Di-8-ANEPPS cathodic polarization reached 66 +- 15% (710 +- 200 mV), so the 600-mV maximum is not the dye's limit.
outcomes.quote: Polarization measured this way reached 66 ± 15% (710 ± 200 mV) at the cathodic pole, suggesting that the 600-mV maximum, averaged from 60 PEFs, was not the dye limit but the actual IMP
outcomes.notes: Needs the Fig. 4B cells; not in the dandiset. Depends on fig4b-di8-limits.

outcomes.statement: Above 780 V/cm the pole IMP fell progressively with field strength, more at the cathodic pole; at 1400 V/cm the cathodic pole no longer charged and the anodic pole fell to about -30% dF (-330 mV).
outcomes.quote: As the electric field increased further, the IMP reached at the poles progressively decreased, and the reduction was more pronounced at the cathodic pole ... At 1400 V/cm, charging was no longer detectable at the cathodic pole (i.e., the membrane became fully permeable) and dropped to ~30% ΔF (~ −330 mV) at the anodic pole.
outcomes.notes: Needs the Fig. 4B cells at 780 to 1400 V/cm; not in the dandiset.

outcomes.statement: Membrane regions nearer the equator were unaffected by pole electroporation and followed the cosine dependence of the Schwan equation up to 1000 V/cm.
outcomes.quote: Membrane areas closer to the equator ... appeared relatively unaffected and followed the cosine dependence predicted by Schwan formula up to 1000 V/cm (Fig. 4C).
outcomes.notes: Needs the Fig. 4B cells and their IMPC; not in the dandiset.

outcomes.statement: With 0.3-us pulses at higher fields (357 to 3320 V/cm), imaged at 275 ns, the maximum dF was 53 +- 4% (about 600 mV) at both poles, as with 1-us pulses, and the response changed with field strength in the same way.
outcomes.quote: Contrary to the expectations, the results were similar to those with 1-μs pulses in Fig. 4B: the maximum ΔF reached was 53 ± 4% (~600 mV) at both cell poles. The pattern of how the response changed with increasing PEF strength was not different from that with 1-μs PEFs either.
outcomes.notes: Needs the 0.3-us Di-8-ANEPPS escalation (n = 10); every set in the dandiset uses 1-us pulses.

outcomes.statement: With 1 mM Gd3+ the anodic pole charged to -864 +- 44 mV, against -542 +- 57 mV in parallel controls (p < 0.001).
outcomes.quote: Indeed, we found that 1 mM Gd3+ extended the range of membrane charging at the anodic pole down to −864 ± 44 mV (p < 0.001 compared to −542 ± 57 mV in parallel control experiments, Fig. 5A).
outcomes.notes: Needs the Gd3+ (n = 7) and control (n = 5) Di-8-ANEPPS cells; the dandiset holds no Gd3+ experiment and no Di-8-ANEPPS recording.

outcomes.statement: With Gd3+, the measured IMP stayed nearly identical to IMPC down to -780 mV, so the Di-8-ANEPPS calibration holds at high IMPs.
outcomes.quote: Furthermore, measured IMP remained nearly identical to the theoretical IMPC down to −780 mV, indicating that the dye response remained linear and its calibration was valid even at high IMPs.
outcomes.notes: Needs the Gd3+ cells of Fig. 5A; not in the dandiset.

outcomes.statement: At the cathodic pole Gd3+ cells reached 647 +- 44 mV, not significantly above controls, but Gd3+ prevented the decline of IMP with stronger fields.
outcomes.quote: At the cathodic pole, polarization in the presence of Gd3+ reached 647 ± 44 mV, a value not significantly higher than that in the control group without Gd3+. However, Gd3+ prevented the progressive decline in IMP as the electric field was increased.
outcomes.notes: Needs the Gd3+ and control cells of Fig. 5A; not in the dandiset.

outcomes.statement: Gd3+ and control data differ significantly for datapoints with IMPC below -700 mV and above 1200 mV.
outcomes.quote: Differences between Gd3+ and control group data are significant at p < 0.05 or better (2-tailed t-test) for datapoints below −700 mV and above 1200 mV.
outcomes.notes: Needs the Gd3+ and control cells of Fig. 5A; not in the dandiset.

outcomes.statement: By Eq. (2), the effective membrane conductivity barely affects charging while it stays far below cytosol and medium conductivities; a 10-fold rise reduces IMP by about 2% and a 100-fold rise by 12%.
outcomes.quote: its 10-fold increase would go unnoticed, yielding just a ~2% IMP reduction, and a 100-fold increase would reduce IMP by just 12%.
outcomes.notes: Eq. (2) with the constants of Methods 2.3 gives f = 1.49798 for the intact membrane. A 10-fold rise in effective conductivity reduces IMP by 1.33% under reading (a), 1 - f/1.5, and by 1.20% under reading (b), relative to the intact f, both outside 2 +- 0.2%. A 100-fold rise gives 11.87% and 11.75%, within 12 +- 1.2%. A 2% reduction needs a 15.2-fold (a) or 16.2-fold (b) rise. With other radii and membrane thicknesses (5 to 12 um, 4 to 7 nm; a variant, not the criterion) the 10-fold reduction is 0.60 to 2.46%, within 2 +- 0.2% only for 10 um with 4 nm (2.06%) or 12 um with 5 nm (1.98%). The claim uses no recordings, so the outcome says nothing about the dataset. The notebook prints the Eq. (2) curve at 1 to 100000-fold (measured IMP 98.67% of IMPC at 10-fold, 88.13% at 100-fold, 42.62% at 1000-fold, 6.91% at 10000-fold) for comparison with the curve of Fig. 5B; it does not read the figure.

outcomes.statement: For most datapoints, Gd3+ reduced the electroporation-induced effective membrane conductivity 2 to 3-fold.
outcomes.quote: For most datapoints, Gd3+ reduced the electroporation- induced effective conductivity 2–3-fold.
outcomes.notes: Needs the Gd3+ and control datapoints of Fig. 5A, which are not in the dandiset. The calibration it depends on (fig5b-conductivity-calibration) was computed.

outcomes.statement: A single 1-us pulse caused clear Ca2+ entry at 1000 and 1200 V/cm, with the signal elevated through 5 min; the small rise at 780 V/cm was not significant.
outcomes.quote: Exposure to a single 1-μs pulse at escalating field strengths, from 0 to 1200 V/cm established a clear peak of Ca2+ entry at 1000 and 1200 V/ cm, and Ca2+ signal remained elevated through the 5-min observation period (Fig. 6A). A subtle ΔF increase after exposure at 780 V/cm was at the detection limit and not statistically significant.
outcomes.notes: Needs Fluo-4 calcium time series (14 cells, 5-min recordings); the dandiset holds only potentiometric strobe images of 60 frames.

outcomes.statement: After a train of sixty 1-us pulses at 6 Hz, 28% of cells responded strongly at 780 V/cm and nearly all at higher field strengths.
outcomes.quote: A strong Ca2+ response was recorded in 28% of cells exposed at 780 V/cm and in nearly all cells at higher intensities (Fig. 6B).
outcomes.notes: Needs the Fluo-4 recordings of 224 cells after 60-pulse trains; not in the dandiset.

outcomes.statement: At 650 V/cm only 2 cells (5.9%) responded strongly, yet the mean Ca2+ signal at the end of recording differed from zero (p < 0.001) and was marginally higher than at 230 V/cm (p < 0.05).
outcomes.quote: At 650 V/cm, only 2 cells (5.9%) showed a strong response, but the mean Ca2+ signal by the end of recording was significantly different from zero (p < 0.001, one sample t-test) and marginally higher than after exposure at 230 V/cm (p < 0.05, single-tailed t-test).

statistics.about: 650 V/cm mean signal at the end of recording against zero

outcomes.notes: Needs the Fluo-4 recordings at 230 and 650 V/cm; not in the dandiset.

outcomes.statement: The azimuthal profile of a 150 V/cm test pulse given 5 us after a conditioning pulse kept the cosine shape of an undamaged membrane after conditioning pulses up to 1000 V/cm, while after 1200 and 1400 V/cm charging at the poles was markedly reduced.
outcomes.quote: Polarization still followed a cosine function after conditioning PEFs of up to 1000 V/cm. However, 1200 and 1400 V/cm conditioning PEFs markedly hindered charging by the test pulse at cell poles, indicating a persistent membrane permeabilization.
outcomes.notes: The criterion uses the Di-8-ANEPPS two-pulse cells of Fig. 7A (n = 5) with conditioning at 150 to 1400 V/cm. The dandiset's 5-us pairs are two fields of view (c2, c9; 5 cells) stained with FluoVolt (all 72 files name FluoVolt and a FITC filter cube), recorded with 1.00-mm electrodes where the paper states 1.6 mm, with conditioning at 150, 520, 900, 1270 and 1570 V/cm and 20 and 40 frames per set. They are a different experiment, so the claim is not tested on them. Their profiles are shown in the notebook as a variant.

outcomes.statement: Normalized to 150 V/cm, pole polarization during the conditioning pulse fell 1.5 times below linear scaling at 560 V/cm and 2-fold at 760 V/cm, and further at stronger fields (p < 0.01 for every point from 560 V/cm).
outcomes.quote: Actual measurements fell 1.5 times below this line for 560 V/cm PEFs, 2- fold for 760 V/cm PEFs, and diverged further for more intense PEFs (p < 0.01 for all datapoints ≥560 V/cm, one sample t-test).
outcomes.notes: Its data are those of Fig. 4B (Di-8-ANEPPS escalation, n = 5), as the criterion states; not in the dandiset. The dandiset's FluoVolt single-pulse sets (c6, c7) are not those data.

outcomes.statement: A 150 V/cm test pulse 5 us after the conditioning pulse charged the poles as in undamaged cells after conditioning up to 760 V/cm, to about 80% (not significant) after 1000 V/cm, and to about 70% and 50% after 1200 and 1400 V/cm, a persistent permeabilization.
outcomes.source: Figure 7A and 7B, bottom panels; Results 3.7, paragraphs 3 and 5
outcomes.quote: However, 1200 and 1400 V/cm conditioning PEFs markedly hindered charging by the test pulse at cell poles, indicating a persistent membrane permeabilization ... In contrast, measurements 6 μs later (test pulse) did not differ from the control up to 760 V/cm strength of the conditioning PEF; they were at ~80% of the control reading after 1000 V/cm conditioning PEF but the difference was not statistically significant. Still more intense PEFs of 1200 and 1400 V/cm reduced charging by the test pulse to ~70% and ~ 50%, respectively (p < 0.05 and p < 0.01, two-sided t-test).

statistics.about: 1200 V/cm conditioning, test pulse against control
1400 V/cm conditioning, test pulse against control

outcomes.notes: The Fig. 7 Di-8-ANEPPS two-pulse cells (n = 5) are not in the dandiset (see fig7a-cosine-profiles). As a variant only, the dandiset's FluoVolt 5-us pairs measured with the paper's pole measure give a test-pulse response of 70% and 64% of the 150/150 set at the anodic pole after 1270 and 1570 V/cm (mean over 5 cells), while the cathodic values vary between cells from -941 to 1074%, as the uniform dimming of the pulse frames (-10.1% at the control) is larger than the cathodic response (4.5%). With that offset removed, the cathodic response is 90 to 92% after 520 and 900 V/cm, 76% after 1270 and 68% after 1570 V/cm.

outcomes.statement: Within 6 us of the electroporating pulse, effective membrane conductivity at the poles fell by a factor of about 10 (range 7 to 20) for most datapoints; the cathodic pole, more conductive during the pulse, no longer differed from the anodic pole at the test pulse.
outcomes.quote: Fig. 7C shows a profound reduction in the λm,eff within just 6 μs after the electroporating pulse. For most datapoints, it dropped by a factor of 10 (range: 7–20). While the cathodic pole became more conductive than the anodic pole during the electroporating pulse ... no difference between the poles was detected by the test pulse.
outcomes.notes: Depends on fig7b-charging-during-pulse and fig7ab-test-pulse-recovery, both blocked for missing data.

outcomes.statement: After mildly electroporating 570 and 760 V/cm pulses the membrane resealed fully within 6 us; after stronger pulses a residual conductivity increase persisted.
outcomes.quote: For mildly electroporating PEFs of 570 and 760 V/cm, membrane resealed fully (within the accuracy of measurements) within just 6 μs. With more intense PEFs, the residual increased conductivity persisted for at least 6 μs, indicating the formation of more stable membrane lesions.
outcomes.notes: Depends on fig7ab-test-pulse-recovery, blocked for missing data.

findings.statement: The dandiset holds none of the recordings behind the paper's figures. Its 72 files are one FluoVolt experiment of 2023-06-22 in 12 fields of view, single 1-us pulses (2 fields) and pulse pairs at intervals of 1, 5, 25, 125 and 250 us (2 fields each), at 150 to 1570 V/cm. The paper's Di-8-ANEPPS escalations (Figs. 1, 2B to D, 4B to D), its FluoVolt escalation (Figs. 2A, 3, 4A), the Gd3+ experiments (Fig. 5), the Fluo-4 calcium imaging (Fig. 6) and the Di-8-ANEPPS two-pulse recordings at a 5-us interval (Fig. 7) are absent. 31 of the 32 claims cannot be tested.

The dandiset's metadata names the paper as the publication of its data (dcite:IsPublishedIn), but the paper reports no FluoVolt two-pulse experiment and no interval other than 5 us, and its Discussion names varying the interval as future work. The files' descriptions also differ from the paper's Methods on the electrode spacing (1.00 mm against 1.6 mm) and the frames per set (20 sham and 40 pulse against 40 and 60).
The general description in every file gives the inter-pulse intervals as 1, 5, 25 and 125 us, but fields of view c5 and c12 hold pairs at 250 us.

The ImageSeries starting_time holds the Unix time of each set's acquisition (1687481119 to 1687486631 s), the same instant as the file's session_start_time, where NWB defines it as the offset from the session's reference time; every recording thus starts about 53 years after its session.

The pulse protocol of each set (sham, single or paired, amplitudes, interval) is only in the free text of session_description; there is no stimulus or trial table, and no frame is labelled as sham or pulse (the data confirm 20 sham frames, then 40). The field direction, the pixel size and the imaging delay per set are not recorded.

The amplitudes are given in volts (50 to 250 V) and the description lists the field strengths 0.15, 0.52, 0.9, 1.27 and 1.57 kV/cm without mapping them to amplitudes. Read in order, these are not proportional to voltage (5 times the voltage for 10.5 times the field), while the paper states that the current scaled linearly with voltage.

The 12 subjects (CHO_20230622_c1 to c12) are fields of view holding several cells each, some of them touching (29 whole, round cells, 2 or 3 per field of view, are measured in the notebook), and the files do not say which cell was the experiment's cell; the paper reports one cell per experiment.

Subject metadata describe a cell line as an organism, with age P1D and sex U, and the archive's summary gives the species as "Cricetulus griseus - Cricetulus aureus" for NCBITaxon_10029 (Cricetulus griseus).

On the cells, the 40 frames after the sham frames are 13.3 to 16.2% dimmer than sham frames 1 to 19 in the sham sets, with no pulse (9.4 to 16.8% with frame 0 in the baseline), and the per-frame pole dF falls within the pulse frames of the sham sets (by 12.1 and 12.2 points between pulse frames 20-29 and 50-59) and within their baseline (by 15.9 and 16.3 points between frames 1-9 and 10-19). In 65 of the 72 files the first frame is more than 10% dimmer than frames 1 to 19 (median 0.64, range 0.52 to 1.11 over files). This uniform offset enters the paper's collapsed dF measure at both poles.

Results 3.5 states that a 10-fold rise in effective membrane conductivity yields a ~2% IMP reduction by Eq. (2), but Eq. (2) with the constants of Methods 2.3 gives 1.33% (1.20% relative to the intact membrane); a 2% reduction needs a 15- to 16-fold rise. The 100-fold value (12%) agrees.

verifications.by: Independent agent run by CatalystNeuro (same harness, separate context, did not write the notebook)
verifications.reviewed: Round 1. The first executed notebook with the conclusion cells and the summary removed, the helper module and the claims file, with the paper. The verifier checked the dye, electrodes and intervals of all 72 assets in the archive's metadata and recomputed Eq. (2). Its report, transcripts/001516/verifier-1-report.md, gave its own outcome for each claim; all 32 agree with the record. Its points on the descriptive section, answered in the revision, were: F0 included the dimmed frame 0 (B5), now left out, with the effect of keeping it printed; the field direction was taken from the response it then measures (B6), now taken for each set from the other pulse sets of its field of view (it moves by -0.4 to 0.7 degrees); the amplitude-to-field mapping cannot be checked (B7), unchanged and still flagged; and no overlay of the traces on the images was shown (not checked), now added for every measured cell. The overlay showed that touching pairs of cells in c2, c3 and c10, and a stacked pair and a cluster of dim cells in c11, had been measured as one cell each; touching cells are now split (which also adds a touching pair in c12) and objects that are not round are left out, which gives 29 cells in place of 30 and changed the descriptive numbers, none of which decides an outcome.

verifications.by: Independent agent run by CatalystNeuro (same harness, separate context, did not write the notebook)
verifications.reviewed: Round 2. The full re-executed notebook after the round-1 revision, the helper module, the claims file and the record, with the paper. Its report, transcripts/001516/verifier-2-report.md, agrees with all 32 outcomes and checked every number in the conclusions, the summary, the README and the record against the printed outputs. Its points on text, none bearing on an outcome, were answered as follows. The summary (cell 29), the record's finding and the helper docstring said the first frame of every set is dimmer, where only the median was printed; cell 15 now prints the range over files and the count below 0.9 (0.52 to 1.11, 65 of 72), and the three texts say 65 of 72 files. Cell 10 listed touching pairs in c2, c3, c10 and c12 and cell 12 listed c11 too; in the overlay (cell 11) c11 cell 1 touches a cell that is left out, and cell 12 now says so. The finding of kind other gave the 12-point and 16-point falls as first against last 10 frames, now corrected. The fig5b response's by-eye reading of Fig. 5B is removed. The round-1 reasons' cell numbers are given with the current ones in brackets.

entries.name: 001516-semenov-2026
entries.title: Membrane charging and recovery after pulsed electric fields (Semenov et al. 2026)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Semenov, Silkuniene, Silkunas, Pakhomova, Bixler, Ibey, Kochunov and Pakhomov (2026) on dandiset 001516. The dandiset holds a FluoVolt two-pulse experiment in CHO cells, with inter-pulse intervals of 1 to 250 us and fields of 150 to 1570 V/cm, which the paper does not report; none of the recordings behind the paper's figures is in it. The one claim that is a computation from the paper's Eq. (2) is tested, and the dataset's own sets are measured with the paper's pole method.
